chapter_name: Chapter 08: Verbs Action, Helping, and Auxiliary
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will distinguish between Main Action Verbs and Helping/Auxiliary Verbs, understanding how they work together in a sentence.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 If a sentence is a car, the Verb is the engine! 🚗 It makes the sentence GO. Sometimes the engine is doing all the work, and sometimes it needs a little help. Let's explore the world of Action and Helping Verbs!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Action verbs tell us what the subject is doing. These can be physical actions that you can see, or mental actions that happen in your head.
Helping verbs do exactly what their name says—they help the main verb! They come before the main verb to show the time of the action (tense) or its possibility.
examples_or_templates: is, am, are, was, were, has, have, had.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Modals are a special type of helping verb that express ability, permission, or necessity. They never change their form.
examples_or_templates: can, could, may, might, must, should.
You MUST wear a helmet. I CAN swim.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the main action verb in this sentence: 'The chef is cooking a delicious meal.'
❓ Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb in this sentence? 'They have finished their homework.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the helping verb and circle the main verb: 'The dog was barking all night.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which word is the actual noise, and which word tells us it happened in the past?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a suitable modal verb: 'You ______ ask the teacher before going out.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of a word that shows asking for permission or an obligation (e.g., must, should, may).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a sentence using a mental action verb.
subjective_practice.hint: Use words like believe, remember, or imagine.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎭 The Mime Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down 5 action verbs on chits of paper. Pick one and act it out without speaking. Ask a family member to guess the verb and use it in a sentence with a helping verb (e.g., 'You ARE JUMPING!').

chapter_summary: ⭐ Main Action verbs express physical or mental activities.
⭐ Helping (Auxiliary) verbs support the main verb to show tense or meaning.
⭐ Modals are special helping verbs showing ability, permission, or obligation.
